questions_and_answers.question_text: How may an "or" question be asked in Chinese?
What must appear in each alternative of this kind of "or" question?
What are the two usual translations of dōu?
What part of speech is dōu, and where must it be placed?
Write the Chinese for "All of them are girls."
When is dōu translated as "both" rather than "all"?

answers.answer_text: When it refers to only two things.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which other adverb takes the same position as dōu?

answers.answer_text: Yě, "also" — both come after the subject and before the verb.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese question meaning "Are they boys or girls?"
Give the Chinese for "Two are here, and one is still in America."

answers.answer_text: Liǎngge zài zhèli, yíge hái zài Měiguó.

articles.text:
5. B: Shì nánháizi, shì nǚháizi?           Are they boys or girls?
   A: Tāmen dōu shi nǚháizi.                All of them are girls.

6. B: Hú Xiānsheng, Hú Tàitai ne?           How about Mr. and Mrs. Hú? How
      Tāmen yǒu jǐge háizi?                 many children do they have?
   A: Tāmen yǒu liǎngge háizi.              They have two children.
   B: Shì nánháizi, shì nǚháizi?            Are they boys or girls?
   A: Dōu shi nǚháizi.                      Both of them are girls.

7. A: Nǐmen háizi dōu zài zhèli ma?         Are all your children here?
   B: Bù, liǎngge zài zhèli, yíge           No. Two are here, and one is still
      hái zài Měiguó.                       in America.

Notes on Nos. 5-7

Shì nánháizi, shì nǚháizi? In Chinese, an "or" question (i.e., a question asking which of two alternatives is true) may be asked simply by stating the two alternatives with a pause between. In this kind of "or" question, the verb must appear in each alternative. (You will learn other ways of making "or" questions in later modules.)

Dōu may usually be translated in a sentence as "all (of)," or, if it refers to only two things, as "both (of)." Literally, dōu means "in all cases," "uniformly," "entirely," "completely." Since it is an adverb, it must be placed after the subject of a sentence and before the verb (like the adverb yě, "also").
